meta.title_tag: Six weeks of warning on a 13bn euro deal
meta.headline: Our partners were briefed on a €13bn takeover six weeks before the market called it.
meta.sub: Uber's bid for Delivery Hero broke on 15 July 2026. Most of the individual signals were public and easy to miss. We sequenced the behavioural pattern, the hiring, the positioning and the market reaction, to work out what was coming and roughly when.
meta.told: A cross-border public bid of this size runs for months on competition filings across many jurisdictions, remedy design around the overlapping markets, and integration planning for technology, logistics and shared functions. That work starts at announcement, not at close.
meta.todo: Approach corporate development at both groups with separation planning and carve-out readiness while regulatory review runs. A 14-market divestment was already pre-agreed, so the carve-out perimeter was knowable before the market had priced it.
meta.strap: We did not break this story. We assembled it.

events.text: Delivery Hero hires a senior antitrust and trade lawyer
First reports Uber is studying a full takeover
Uber weighs raising its offer; shares climb 10%
An antitrust hire alongside takeover chatter is a preparation pattern. We sequenced it and gave partners the angle and the window
Structure narrows to the regional businesses

Uber bids €41.50 a share,
valuing Delivery Hero near €13bn

meta.title_tag: Five weeks ahead of a 5.7bn take-private
meta.headline: We tracked a £5.7bn take-private from first rumour to final bid.
meta.sub: Castlelake's interest in easyJet surfaced on 30 May 2026. It was on our board the next day. We read the behaviour, not the headline: a rejected approach that keeps returning with a higher number is a pattern we track, and it told us terms were coming well before they did.
meta.for_work:
Take-private structuring
Regulatory and slot analysis
100-day value creation
meta.told: A contested airline take-private drives ownership-and-control structuring against EU nationality rules, slot and regulatory analysis, debt financing diligence, and a 100-day value creation plan spanning fleet, loyalty and the holidays business.
meta.todo: £10.1bn of revenue and positive pre-tax profit, against a bid vehicle where the sponsor holds only 49% alongside EU-national investors. Brief the sponsor's aviation deal team and the target's chief commercial officer on holidays attach-rate and ancillary revenue upside.
meta.strap: Four rejections. Two bidders. One sequence.

events.text: A US private credit firm is reported to be circling
An opportunistic approach into a depressed share price, the profile that historically precedes a repeat bidder. On the board next morning
easyJet calls the timing opportunistic; shares jump 10%
A second suitor is reported to be interested
Third proposal rejected; bidder goes direct to shareholders

Board agrees terms.
Rival bid follows at £5.7bn

meta.title_tag: Five weeks inside Europe's biggest bank fight
meta.headline: We had partners inside the €39bn bank fight five weeks before its endgame.
meta.sub: A public rebuff, a regulator complaint, a government rejection, and the stake rising anyway. We sequenced the behaviour, not the headlines. An acquirer that keeps buying through every obstacle is telling you how this ends, months before the market prices it.
meta.for_work:
Regulatory and ECB strategy
Political and works council engagement
Contingency integration
meta.told: Whether or not full control follows, both banks need work now: ECB approval strategy, a German political and stakeholder plan given the federal shareholding and works council opposition, and contingency integration planning covering corporate lending, payments and deposits overlap.
meta.todo: Only a small share of acceptances came from independent institutional and retail investors, which tells you the minority base is unconvinced and the governance fight is not over. Offer both sides parallel scenario work rather than betting on one outcome.
meta.strap: Nobody missed the deal. Everybody missed the build-up.

events.text: Commerzbank's chief executive publicly rebuffs the approach
Rebuffed in public yet still accumulating stock. That behaviour rarely reverses, so we surfaced it at confidence 88
The bank contacts the German regulator over the stake build
The stake is lifted to 42.5% regardless
